clue.text: Absolutely final way to get petrol during part of Grand Prix?

indicators.note: one thing happening during another sits within it, so these letters go inside the lap

parts.note: a lap is one circuit of a motor race such as a Grand Prix
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
gas is the American word for petrol

explanation.surface: A racing driver pits for fuel in the middle of a lap of a Grand Prix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' is the insertion signal; 'to get' only links the way to the fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A last gasp is a final effort or moment, so something done at the last gasp comes at the very end.

clue.text: Body of water cheers navy

parts.note: ta is informal British thanks, as is cheers
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A toast raised to the navy beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarn is a small mountain lake, a kind of body of water.

clue.text: Still to go North during end of day, not South

indicators.note: not South says the letter for South is dropped
North comes during the end of day, so its letter goes inside it

parts.note: sunset is the end of the day

explanation.surface: Instructions to head north at dusk rather than south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' puts N into SUNSET, making SUNSENT; 'not' then removes the first S.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter still to go has not yet been dispatched, so it remains unsent.

clue.text: Whisky maker often caught coming in drunk

indicators.note: the caught letter comes into the word for a drunk, so it sits inside

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunk
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A distiller is often arrested arriving home drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming in' puts C inside SOT. Scotch whisky is made in Scotland, so a Scot is often a whisky maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland is the home of Scotch whisky, so a Scottish person is often the one who distils it.

clue.text: Pointer, perhaps warning better used about Government

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shouted warning

indicators.note: the finer word goes about the letter for Government, enclosing it

parts.note: finer means better

explanation.surface: Advice that a warning works better when it is aimed at the Government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts G inside FINER.
explanation.definitionFit: The forefinger is the index finger, the digit used for pointing, so it is an example of a pointer.

clue.text: Piece still lacking odd bits, in the event

indicators.note: the remaining letters are placed in the word for the event

parts.note: case means event, as in 'in that case'

indicators.note: dropping the odd-placed letters keeps only the even ones of still

explanation.surface: A chess piece stays still, missing a few odd bits, in the event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking odd bits' keeps the even letters of 'still'; 'in' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle is a chess piece, also called a rook.

clue.text: Mother taking husband into desert for test of endurance

parts.note: ma is mother

indicators.note: the husband's letter is taken into the word for desert, inside it

parts.note: to rat on someone is to desert or betray them

explanation.surface: A mother drags her husband into the desert for a gruelling trek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like sand but is the verb meaning abandon; 'taking ... into' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A marathon is a long-distance race, and figuratively any long, exhausting task that tests stamina.

clue.text: Veggie fan? That woman's drill involves one source of veganism

parts.note: her refers to that woman

indicators.note: the drill word involves, or takes in, the other letters

parts.note: to bore is to drill
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A vegetarian enthusiast's drill bit features something from veganism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involves' signals the insertion; 'source of veganism' gives its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbivore eats plants only, so jokingly it is a fan of vegetables.

clue.text: Church examination for singers …

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A church audition held for choir members.
explanation.definitionFit: Choral music is written for a choir, so it is for singers.

clue.text: … such as me and nine more men?

parts.note: the setter plus nine others makes ten
OR, other ranks, are soldiers or men

explanation.surface: The setter, continuing the previous clue, imagines himself among ten men in a choir.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to the previous clue's singers: the setter casts himself as one.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is a male singing voice, so the setter claims to be one of those singers.

clue.text: Petition to refuse ousting leader about indulgence

indicators.note: the trimmed word goes round, or about, the indulgence
ousting its leader drops the first letter of the word

parts.note: to deny is to refuse
a treat is an indulgence

explanation.surface: A petition rejected for opposing some privilege.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ousting leader' drops a first letter and 'about' wraps the result round the indulgence.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest request or plea, the same thing as a petition.

clue.text: Glean enteritis inflamed — my neighbour?

indicators.note: inflamed letters are agitated and so rearranged

explanation.surface: Bowel inflammation spoken of by a neighbouring organ.
explanation.walkthrough: The speaker is presumably the small intestine, whose neighbour is the larger one; enteritis is an inflamed intestine, so the surface fits.
explanation.definitionFit: The small intestine leads straight into the large one, so the two organs are neighbours in the gut.

clue.text: Look at a floodgate, ruined

indicators.note: ruined letters are wrecked and so rearranged

explanation.surface: A gaze at a wrecked floodgate.
explanation.definitionFit: Get a load of is a slang command to look at something remarkable.

clue.text: Say nothing with Phi's messy copy being tidied up

parts.note: sh is a call for silence

indicators.note: messy letters are jumbled and so rearranged

parts.note: to ape is to copy

explanation.surface: The setter Phi stays quiet while his messy copy is tidied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messy' rearranges PHIS into IPSH.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipshape means neat and orderly, as a vessel kept tidy would be.

clue.text: Customer runs into no bar backwards

indicators.note: runs goes into the reversed words, inside them
read backwards, the words no bar are turned round

parts.note: a tap is a bar, as in taproom
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A customer storms into a bar that refuses service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backwards' turns NOTAP into PATON; 'into' puts R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron is a regular customer of a shop, pub or restaurant.

clue.text: Crime happily avoiding boy without companions?

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing, a crime

indicators.note: avoiding the boy means his letters are removed

parts.note: gladly means happily
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Happily committing a crime while dodging a boy, all alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' takes LAD out of GLADLY, leaving GLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Done singly means one at a time or individually, so with no companions.

clue.text: American greeting English newspaper turning up in US National Park

parts.note: yo is an American greeting

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up reads the words from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: The Times is a newspaper

explanation.surface: An American greets an English newspaper appearing in a national park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses ETIMES to SEMITE, after YO.
explanation.definitionFit: Yosemite is a famous national park in California's Sierra Nevada.

clue.text: Dance item possibly a strain for dance specialist

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be in another order

parts.note: stress is a strain

explanation.surface: One dance number might strain the performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges ITEM into ETMI.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballet mistress trains and rehearses the dancers of a ballet company, so she is a dance specialist.

clue.text: Reckon year with investment of gold is a good one

indicators.note: investment is putting something in, so gold goes inside the reckoning word

parts.note: to bet is to reckon, as in I bet he's late
AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Judging that investing in gold this year is a good one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investment of' signals the insertion: gold is invested in the bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A beauty is informal for a fine example of something, a good one.

clue.text: Crazy being irritable after losing paint

indicators.note: the word is what remains after losing the paint word

parts.note: temperamental means moody and irritable
tempera is a kind of paint

explanation.surface: Someone driven mad by moods after a paint pot goes missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after losing' signals the deletion of the paint from the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Mental is informal for mad or crazy.

clue.text: Fuel problem keeps airmen fidgeting initially

indicators.note: the problem word keeps, or holds, the other letters inside it

parts.note: a pain is a nuisance, a problem
the RAF is the Royal Air Force, its airmen

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fuel problem leaves pilots fidgeting at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' signals the insertion; 'initially' takes the first letter of 'fidgeting'.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraffin is kerosene, an oil burned as fuel in lamps and heaters.

clue.text: Congregation to collapse

explanation.definitionFit: Fold means both a body of believers, from the sheepfold image, and to give way or collapse.

clue.text: Tracks almost completely dreadful

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: all means completely
bum is British slang for bad or dreadful, as in a bum note

explanation.surface: Musical tracks nearly all awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts ALL to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: An album is a collection of recorded tracks, so the tracks stand for it.

clue.text: Descriptive prose not entirely an illegible mess?

indicators.note: not entirely says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a blurb is a short descriptive piece of prose on a book jacket

explanation.surface: A book jacket's text is half finished and an unreadable mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' cuts BLURB to BLUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A blur is something indistinct, and smudged writing that can't be read is one.

clue.text: Small problem on the internet? No great rush

parts.note: a troll posts provocative messages online, a problem on the internet

explanation.surface: A minor online nuisance is nothing to hurry over.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroll is a leisurely walk, the opposite of a rush.

clue.text: Present time allocated to match is satisfactory

parts.note: AD, anno domini, labels the present era
to equate is to match

explanation.surface: The time given to a sports match is enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Adequate means good enough, sufficient for the purpose.
